{"concern":"core","designation":"internal","kind":"functional","lineage":"original","name":"The build loop is bounded, and exhausting the budget forces a return to the design","priority":"medium","provenance":"authored","statement":"reflow2 MEASURES design erosion under repeated build rounds and never BOUNDS it. tools/ carries the erosion trial whose stated question is "not 'did a file change?' but: after N rounds of test-fails/fix-code/accept, does the design still describe what it should" — so the decay is known, quantified, and regression-gated. Nothing, however, ever says STOP. A session can iterate test-fix indefinitely and reflow2 will report the drift afterwards rather than interrupt it.

THE PRIOR ART, from reflow's workflow_master.json: iteration_budgets carries P3_P4_loops = 3 and P4_P3_loops = 3, and on_budget_exceeded triggers the resync protocol with target_phase P2 and escalate_to_P1_if "drift_score > 0.5". So after three build-test rounds work HALTS and the agent is sent back up to architecture — or further, to functional analysis, if the drift is bad enough. The resync protocol itself is six ordered steps: halt_current_work, detect_drift, present_comparison, mode_specific_resolution, reset_iteration_counter, continue_or_escalate.

THE BUDGET WAS ASKED FOR, NOT ASSUMED — AMENDED 2026-07-28, same day, after reviewing workflows/phases/. The 3 above is a DEFAULT, not a constant: workflows/phases/P0_setup/phase_definition.json puts the question to the user during setup — "How many development/test iterations before forced architecture review?", default 3, range 1 to 10 — alongside the mode choice and, for rigid projects, the acceptable drift level. That matters for two reasons. It removes the obvious objection that 3 is arbitrary: it is this project's answer to a question every project was asked. And it sets the shape reflow2 should copy — the bound is a per-project value elicited once, not a constant compiled in, which is the same distinction ver:interface-spec draws between a default that records absence and one that names a choice.

DISTINCT FROM cap:budget, which rolls up a RESOURCE budget against a Constraint (mass, cost, power). This is an ITERATION budget on the design process itself, and reflow2 has no vocabulary for it.

NOT MERELY A PHASE-MODEL ARTEFACT, which is the objection to expect: the mechanism is about work that does NOT terminate. A bounded loop with a forced return upward is precisely the discipline a continual evolution effort needs — Anthony's framing of design as (1) define the current state, (2) evolve it incrementally, with no clean start or exit criteria. The budget is what stops "evolve incrementally" from becoming "drift indefinitely while the graph records it faithfully." Supporting evidence from the same review: reflow's own P5_operations phase_definition states that "P5 is typically ongoing" and routes production issues back_to_P3_P4 as "a new development cycle", so even the phase model this came from did not assume termination.

Whether the trigger should be a loop COUNT (reflow's answer) or a measured drift threshold, or both, is open — reflow used both, counting loops and escalating on drift_score, with both thresholds elicited per project. Found 2026-07-28 reviewing the original reflow workflows. Anthony's word: capture it.","status":"proposed"}
